title: Curaçao Jewish Heritage Journey
subtitle: Join Rabbi Joel Sisenwine and TBE congregant and Curaçao native Susan Alvares Correa as we embark on a remarkable journey to Curaçao, a Caribbean island with an extraordinary Jewish heritage, vibrant culture, and breathtaking beauty.
leader: Rabbi Joel Sisenwine & Susan Alvares Correa
pace: Guided touring most days 9:00 AM–3:00 PM, with leisure afternoons
accommodation: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad
price_note: Pricing and booking details will be shared once the program is finalized. Registering your interest is not a booking.
intro:
Join Rabbi Joel Sisenwine and TBE congregant and Curaçao native Susan Alvares Correa as we embark on a remarkable journey to Curaçao, a Caribbean island with an extraordinary Jewish heritage, vibrant culture, and breathtaking beauty.

Together, we’ll meet members of today’s Jewish community, explore the people and places that shaped this enduring legacy, share Shabbat and Havdalah, and taste the flavors and traditions that have been passed down through generations. We’ll also venture into Bandabou, rural Curaçao, to encounter Curaçao’s Afro-Curaçaoan history, art, and music, placing the island’s Jewish story within the broader cultural and historical landscape in which it developed.

From the historic Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue—home to the oldest continuously active Jewish congregation in the Americas—to centuries-old Jewish cemeteries, historic family homes, and the colorful streets of Willemstad, we’ll trace more than 375 years of Jewish life and reflect on a unique Jewish legacy that continues to thrive.
highlights:
Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue — the Snoa, oldest continuously operating synagogue in the Americas
Kabbalat Shabbat at the Snoa and an outdoor Shabbat dinner
Beth Haim Blenheim, the oldest Jewish cemetery in the Caribbean (1659)
Bandabou: the Tula Museum, artist Yubi Kirindongo and percussionist Pernell Saturnino
Havdalah on the beach and dinner in a historic Otrobanda gallery
Hosted throughout by Hannah Berkeley Cohen of L'Dor Vador Travel
included:
Five nights at the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad
Breakfast daily at the resort
Meals where indicated in the itinerary (welcome dinner, Day 2 lunch, Day 3 lunch and Shabbat dinner, Day 4 gallery dinner, farewell dinner)
All guided touring, entrances, private encounters and transportation as described
Hosting throughout by Hannah Berkeley Cohen of L'Dor Vador Travel
not_included:
International airfare (participants book their own flights)
Airport transfers (assistance available on request)
Meals not indicated in the itinerary
Optional excursions on the free day
Travel insurance and gratuities
notes:
Flights: International airfare is not included in the group arrangements. Participants book their own flights, providing maximum flexibility to arrive early, extend their stay, or continue onward after Curaçao.
Travel Assistance: Participants who would like assistance with flights or airport transfers may contact Hannah Berkeley Cohen of L’Dor Vador Travel, who will also serve as a host throughout the journey.
Hotel: The group program is based at the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort in Willemstad.
Meals: Breakfast is included daily at the resort. Other meals are included where specifically indicated in the itinerary.
Program Flexibility: The itinerary reflects the planned program. Specific speakers, hosts, cultural figures, and private encounters are subject to availability. Should any featured individual be unavailable during the group’s visit, L’Dor Vador Travel will arrange a suitable and equally compelling alternative whenever possible.
Optional Programming: Additional programming with Rabbi Joel and/or Susan may be offered during periods designated as leisure time and will be communicated to participants on the island.

itinerary.title: Arrival in the Crossroads of the Caribbean
itinerary.text:
Individual Arrivals in Curaçao
Welcome to Curaçao! Participants arrive individually and make their way to the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort in Willemstad for check-in.

Our journey officially begins at the hotel, allowing participants the flexibility to select the flights and travel arrangements that work best for them. Participants are therefore welcome to arrive in Curaçao earlier, extend their stay after the program, or continue onward to another destination.

For those who would like assistance, Hannah Berkeley Cohen of L’Dor Vador Travel, our host throughout the journey, will be available to assist participants individually with flight arrangements and airport transfers.

After check-in, take some time to settle in, relax at the resort, and enjoy your first views of the Caribbean.

18:15 — Welcome Dinner & Orientation
This evening, we come together for the first time at Gouverneur Restaurant for our welcome dinner and orientation.

Meet your fellow travelers and hosts as we introduce the journey ahead and set the stage for our exploration of Curaçao’s remarkable Jewish, Caribbean, and multicultural heritage.
itinerary.summary: Participants arrive individually and make their way to the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort in Willemstad. Our journey officially begins at the hotel, with flexibility to arrive early or extend your stay. We come together this evening at Gouverneur Restaurant for our welcome dinner and orientation.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: The Sephardic Story of Curaçao
itinerary.text:
Touring: 9:00 AM–3:00 PM

09:00 — Historic Willemstad
We begin with a drive through Willemstad, a UNESCO World Heritage city renowned for its distinctive and colorful colonial architecture.

Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue — The Snoa
Continue to Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue, affectionately known as the Snoa. Completed in 1732, it is the oldest continuously operating synagogue in the Americas and connects us to a Sephardic Jewish story whose Spanish and Portuguese roots can be traced to the Iberian Peninsula of the 1400s. Here, we meet Rabbi Martin Hirsch and enjoy a presentation by Ron Gomes Casseres, a Jewish historian in Curaçao.

Jewish Museum Curaçao
After sampling kesito, a traditional Curaçaoan Sephardic cookie, we continue into the Jewish Museum Curaçao. Explore the museum at your own pace with an audio tour, or choose to join a highlights tour with curator Phyllis Meit.

Lunch at La Vie en Rose
We head to La Vie en Rose, operated by Le Cordon Bleu alumnus Luigi Chavarria and his partner Patricia Loggetto, for a private high-tea-style lunch. The restaurant is located in historic Scharloo, known for its elegant colonial mansions, many of which were once owned by prosperous Jewish merchants during the 19th century.

Curaçao’s Historic Jewish Cemeteries
On our way back to the hotel, we pass the newer Jewish cemetery, established in 1864, as well as historic Beth Haim Blenheim Cemetery. Established in 1659 by Curaçao’s first 12 Jewish families, Beth Haim Blenheim is the oldest Jewish cemetery in the Caribbean. Its richly carved tombstones preserve the story of Curaçao’s early Sephardic community and its far-reaching Atlantic connections.

Afternoon & Evening at Leisure
The remainder of the afternoon and evening is yours to enjoy at leisure. Optional programming with Rabbi Joel and/or Susan will be shared once we are all on the island. Dinner is on your own this evening; recommendations will be provided.
itinerary.summary: We visit the historic Mikvé Israel-Emanuel Synagogue — the Snoa, completed in 1732 and the oldest continuously operating synagogue in the Americas — followed by the Jewish Museum Curaçao and a private lunch in historic Scharloo. On the way back we pass Curaçao’s historic Jewish cemeteries, including Beth Haim Blenheim, established in 1659.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Legacies in Art, Architecture & Culture
itinerary.text:
Touring: 9:00 AM–3:00 PM | Evening Program: 5:00–8:00 PM

09:00 — Art, Heritage & Culture Tour
Today, we set out on an on-and-off bus exploration of Curaçao’s Jewish legacy, art, architecture, and cultural heritage.

Mongui Maduro Historic House
Visit this meticulously preserved historic plantation house and discover the legacy of the Levy Maduro family, a prominent Sephardic Jewish lineage that significantly influenced Curaçao’s economic and social landscape over four generations.

Chobolobo Distillery
Discover the history and production of Curaçao’s iconic Blue Curaçao liqueur, invented by a local Sephardic Jewish family. We also sample a crescent-shaped, deep-fried pastry similar to an empanada and commonly found throughout the Dutch Caribbean.

Landhuis Bloemhof & Cathedral of Thorns
Continue to Landhuis Bloemhof, today a cultural center dedicated to art, heritage, and nature. Learn about the history and ideals of the family that has continued to innovate at Bloemhof across generations. Visit the extraordinary Cathedral of Thorns, conceived as a space for reflection and healing and as a powerful metaphor for Curaçao’s complex history, including colonialism and slavery.

Lunch at Number Ten
Enjoy lunch together at Number Ten.

Afternoon at Leisure
Following lunch, we return to our resort for time to rest and enjoy the property. Optional programming with Rabbi Joel and/or Susan will be shared once we are all on the island.

17:00 — Kabbalat Shabbat
As the sun begins to set, we come together for Kabbalat Shabbat at the Snoa.

Shabbat Dinner
Following services, return to the resort for an outdoor Shabbat dinner, celebrating the arrival of Shabbat together in Curaçao.
itinerary.summary: We tour Curaçao’s Jewish legacy in art and architecture — the Mongui Maduro Historic House, Chobolobo Distillery, and Landhuis Bloemhof with its Cathedral of Thorns — followed by lunch at Number Ten. As the sun sets we gather for Kabbalat Shabbat at the Snoa, then return to the resort for an outdoor Shabbat dinner.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Afro-Curaçaoan Heritage, Art & Identity
itinerary.text:
Bandabou | Immersive Afro-Curaçaoan History, Art & Music Day Program: 9:00 AM–4:00 PM | Evening Program from 6:30 PM

09:00 — Depart for Bandabou
Travel west into Bandabou, Curaçao’s rural western region, where plantation history, Afro-Curaçaoan traditions, and the island’s struggle for freedom remain deeply embedded in the landscape.

10:00 — Tula Museum at Landhuis Kenepa
Visit the Tula Museum, housed at the former Kenepa plantation, one of the principal sites associated with Curaçao’s great slave revolt of 1795. We are personally welcomed by Jeanne Henriquez, historian, activist, and director of the museum. Through the story of Tula, leader of the 1795 uprising and today recognized as a national hero of Curaçao, Jeanne introduces us to the history of slavery, resistance, emancipation, and the continuing process of confronting Curaçao’s colonial past.

12:00 — Santa Cruz & Captain Goodlife
Continue approximately ten minutes to Santa Cruz, a secluded beach nestled within one of Bandabou’s beautiful natural coves. Stop at the legendary home base of Juni “Captain Goodlife” Obersi and refresh with a cocktail on the shaded terrace overlooking the bay, or enjoy a leisurely stroll along the beach.

13:30 — Art, Rhythm & Curaçaoan Identity: Yubi Kirindongo & Pernell Saturnino
Continue to the extraordinary home and atelier of internationally renowned Curaçaoan artist Yubi Kirindongo, known for transforming discarded materials into powerful works of art rooted in Curaçao, the African diaspora, and social consciousness. We are joined by Pernell Saturnino, Grammy Award-winning percussionist and Berklee College of Music alumnus, who introduces us to traditional Afro-Curaçaoan rhythms and instruments, including the tambú and chapi. Drinks and finger food are served during this intimate afternoon gathering.

18:30 — Sunset Community Time & Havdalah
Gather on the resort beach as the sun sets over the Caribbean Sea. Share community time followed by Havdalah, marking the transition from Shabbat into the new week.

19:15 — Art, Books & Dinner in Historic Otrobanda
Walk together through historic Otrobanda to Sebastopol 9, an art gallery housed in a monumental 18th-century residence that has remained in the same family for approximately three centuries. Enjoy a private catered dinner buffet inside the gallery, surrounded by contemporary local art. During the evening, meet Anneroos Reich, an active member of Curaçao’s Jewish community and a board member of the Jewish Museum, who will open her bookstore Hirsch & Reich after hours for our group.
itinerary.summary: We travel into Bandabou to visit the Tula Museum, meeting historian Jeanne Henriquez, then the home and atelier of artist Yubi Kirindongo with percussionist Pernell Saturnino. We close the day with Havdalah on the resort beach and a private dinner at the Sebastopol 9 gallery in historic Otrobanda.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Curaçao at Your Own Pace
itinerary.text:
Day at Leisure | Farewell Dinner in the Evening

A Day to Explore, Discover or Simply Relax
Our final full day in Curaçao is intentionally left free of scheduled programming, allowing everyone to experience the island at their own pace. Take a self-guided exploratory walk through Willemstad’s historic center, return to Hirsch & Reich Bookstore for a last-minute book or souvenir, or simply relax beside the resort’s infinity pool and enjoy its sweeping sea views. Those who would like to explore farther afield may choose from a variety of optional excursions and activities. Suggestions will be offered by your hosts.

Farewell Dinner
On our final night in Curaçao, we come together for a festive open-air farewell dinner at our resort. Over dinner, we reflect on the people we have met, the stories we have encountered, and all that we have experienced together during our Caribbean journey.
itinerary.summary: Our final full day is intentionally left free of scheduled programming, so everyone can experience the island at their own pace — Willemstad’s historic center, the infinity pool, or an optional excursion. We close with a festive open-air farewell dinner at the resort.
itinerary.overnight: Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort, Willemstad

itinerary.title: Farewell to Curaçao
itinerary.text:
Departure Day

Individual Departures
Our shared journey concludes at the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort. Participants depart according to their individual travel arrangements. Those extending their stay in Curaçao or continuing onward to another destination are free to do so according to their own schedules.

Hannah Berkeley Cohen of L’Dor Vador Travel will be available to assist participants with their individual airport transfers and onward travel arrangements.
itinerary.summary: Our shared journey concludes at the Renaissance Wind Creek Curaçao Resort. Participants depart according to their individual travel arrangements, whether extending their stay or continuing onward. Hannah Berkeley Cohen will be available to assist with airport transfers and onward travel.
